gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Marantz MODEL 60n's HDMI ARC plays TV sound only when the TV is set to 'PCM 2ch', and that Marantz warns Dolby Digital, DTS or AAC sent into it 'causes noise and could damage the speakers'. The NAD C 3050's eARC port also needs the TV set to 'PCM only'. The Marantz MODEL M1 decodes Dolby Digital and Dolby Digital+ itself.
standout_why: I opened the cited Marantz MODEL M1 US page. It lists 'HDMI eARC' and 'Decoding Dolby Digital +, Dolby Digital, LPCM, DSD' but says nothing about what TV setting the other amps need. ChatGPT's answer only says ARC/eARC is 'primarily for receiving audio from your TV' and recommends the 60n with no format warning. I could not open the cited audiolab.com and nadelectronics.com pages: both returned HTTP 429 on three tries, including through storecheck. So I can't rule out that they carry the PCM note. They are store pages, and the NAD instruction appears in its owner's manual, so it is unlikely to be on them. The M1 infosheet PDF did not yield readable text.
decides: For a TV-first buyer this favours the Marantz MODEL M1, the only candidate whose maker documents say it decodes Dolby Digital and Dolby Digital+ from the TV. The MODEL 60n and NAD C 3050 still work, but the TV's digital-audio output has to be switched to PCM. On the 60n, Marantz warns that leaving it on Dolby, DTS or AAC risks noise and speaker damage. On the Audiolab 7000A, Ed Selley found the ARC link sometimes didn't lock with the TV and wouldn't turn the amp on or off with the screen.

findings.label: TV audio format required over HDMI ARC
findings.value: PCM 2ch only. Marantz: 'Only the PCM 2-channel setting can be used to play sound from a TV via the HDMI ARC function. Set "PCM 2ch" as the audio format in the TV settings.'
findings.source_title: Marantz MODEL 60n online manual (NA): Connecting to a device with digital audio connectors
findings.note: This is the maker's North American manual. The EU page has the same wording.

findings.label: Excluded input formats and stated risk
findings.value: Dolby Digital, DTS and AAC must not be sent in. Marantz: 'Do not input non-PCM signals, such as Dolby Digital, DTS and AAC. This causes noise and could damage the speakers.'
findings.source_title: Marantz MODEL 60n online manual (NA): Connecting to a device with digital audio connectors
findings.note: The warning is on the same manual page as the HDMI ARC and optical/coaxial instructions. The manual also says to use optical or coaxial if the TV lacks ARC.

findings.label: TV audio format required over HDMI eARC
findings.value: PCM only. NAD: 'Ensure that the audio setting/format of eARC-connected devices to C 3050 is set to PCM only.'
findings.source_title: NAD C3050 Stereophonic Amplifier Manual (ManualsLib mirror of NAD owner's manual)
findings.note: This is a mirror of NAD's owner's manual; nadelectronics.com returned HTTP 429. The same manual says the eARC port carries 'Only audio output signal from TV', with no video output. It recommends an Ultra High-Speed certified HDMI cable.

findings.label: Power on/off with the TV (CEC Power)
findings.value: Supported and switchable. 'CEC Power allows the C 3050 to be powered up or down by an external TV connected via HDMI eARC port.' To toggle it, hold the front HDMI button until the HDMI Source LED flashes: twice means enabled, once means disabled.
findings.source_title: NAD C3050 Stereophonic Amplifier Manual (ManualsLib mirror of NAD owner's manual)
findings.note: The TV must support HDMI Control (CEC) and eARC, per the same manual.

findings.label: Formats decoded from the TV over eARC
findings.value: Dolby Digital+, Dolby Digital, LPCM, DSD. Both stereo and multichannel PCM are listed as Yes. DTS is not listed.
findings.source_title: MODEL M1 - 2 Channel 100W Wireless Streaming Amplifier Powered by HEOS | Marantz - United States
findings.note: Spec rows: 'Digital Inputs HDMI (eARC), TOSLINK' and '1x HDMI eARC'. The page lists no phono input. US price on the page is $1,000.

findings.label: Fallback for TVs without eARC/ARC
findings.value: Optical. 'When connecting to a TV that does not support the eARC/ARC function, use an optical connection to play the TV audio.' Marantz also says to turn off the TV's internal speakers.
findings.source_title: Marantz MODEL M1 online manual: Connecting a digital device
findings.note: This page has no PCM-only instruction, unlike the MODEL 60n page.

findings.label: HDMI ARC power and lock behaviour (named reviewer)
findings.value: Ed Selley: the HDMI ARC connection 'sometimes didn't lock with the TV and won't turn the amp on or off with the screen'. Volume could still be adjusted from the TV remote.
findings.source_title: Audiolab 7000A & 7000CDT review, Sound Advice (Ed Selley, May 2, 2023)
findings.note: The review names no TV model and gives no format list. The 7000A has HDMI ARC, not eARC (spec line: 'HDMI ARC').

unsourced: Audiolab 7000A ARC format list (PCM-only or Dolby): Audiolab's manual PDF and its 7000A Product Info Doc PDF both returned compressed content with no readable text, and audiolab.com returned HTTP 429. Only Audio T's retailer copy, seen as a search snippet and not opened, says PCM only.
Whether the cited audiolab.com and nadelectronics.com rival pages mention the PCM requirement: both returned HTTP 429 on every try.
Today's prices for the Audiolab 7000A, NAD C 3050, Marantz MODEL 60n and Onkyo Muse Y-40. The store pages were rate-limited, and the Marantz MODEL 60n US URL I tried returned 404.
Onkyo Muse Y-40 HDMI ARC format support: not researched, because of the call budget.
NAD C 3050 owner's manual on nadelectronics.com itself: blocked by HTTP 429, so I used the ManualsLib mirror.
